sections.070-01: ICAO Annex 6, Part II – Operation of Aircraft

questions.text: In a tricycle-gear aeroplane, which combination particularly encourages wheelbarrowing during the landing roll?
options: Excessive touchdown speed followed by forward elevator pressure
Excessive touchdown speed with the nosewheel held clear
Low touchdown speed with aft elevator pressure
Normal touchdown speed with the nosewheel lowered gently

questions.text: An in-flight engine-compartment fire has been suppressed by securing the engine according to its emergency checklist. Should the pilot restart it merely to see whether it now runs normally?
options: No; an apparently extinguished fire can rekindle and structural damage may remain.
Yes; a successful restart proves there is no remaining fire risk.
Yes; restored oil pressure proves the engine bay is safe.
Yes; if smoke disappears, the normal checklist replaces the emergency procedure.

questions.text: An electrical fire is suspected in flight. The faulty circuit cannot readily be isolated and flight conditions permit removal of electrical power. Which action removes the possible electrical source, subject to the AFM/POH?
options: Turn off the relevant master and generator/alternator supply.
Increase electrical loads until the faulty circuit identifies itself.
Reset all tripped breakers and hold them in.
Turn the cabin heater to maximum while leaving every circuit powered.

questions.text: During a steady approach, a light aeroplane enters a sharp decrease in headwind. Before corrective pilot or automatic-control action, which initial tendency is expected?
options: Airspeed decreases and the aeroplane tends to descend below the intended approach path.
Airspeed increases and the aeroplane tends to climb above the intended path.
Airspeed decreases but lift must remain unchanged.
Airspeed and flight path remain unchanged because the runway has not moved.

questions.text: An aeroplane on a straight approach flies through the centre of a stationary, approximately symmetric microburst. Which sequence of effects explains why an initial improvement can be misleading?
options: Initial headwind/airspeed gain, then downdraught, followed by tailwind/airspeed loss.
Initial tailwind/airspeed loss, then a guaranteed updraught and continuing headwind gain.
Only a steady crosswind, with no vertical airflow.
A permanent increase in airspeed throughout the encounter.

questions.text: Two aeroplanes of the same type fly at the same weight and airspeed. Which configuration normally produces the stronger initial wake vortex?
options: Clean configuration, with gear and flaps retracted.
Landing configuration with gear and flaps extended.
Configuration has no influence if the type and weight are the same.
The configuration having the lower cockpit noise.

questions.text: A pilot decides on a precautionary off-field landing while power and control remain available. What useful opportunity distinguishes this from an immediate forced landing?
options: Time to assess the field, surface, obstacles and a safe approach before committing.
Permission to ignore aircraft limitations during the inspection.
A guarantee that any unprepared field will be smooth enough.
The ability to replace visual inspection with a radio call alone.

questions.text: Which pair correctly distinguishes two landings: one forced by an engine failure, and one deliberately made while further flight remains possible but weather makes continuing unwise?
options: Forced landing; precautionary landing.
Precautionary landing; forced landing.
Ditching; runway incursion.
Normal landing; instrument approach.

questions.text: A light aeroplane relies on wheel brakes when landing. Compared with firm dry pavement, what particular landing hazard can short wet grass create?
options: Reduced tyre adhesion and a longer landing roll.
Guaranteed shorter stopping distance because all grass adds drag.
No effect provided the grass is short.
Improved braking from water lubricating the tyres.

questions.text: Why can appreciable standing water, loose wet snow or slush on a runway reduce acceleration during the take-off roll?
options: Displacing the contaminant adds drag and rolling resistance.
It increases engine thrust through greater runway friction.
It always raises tyre adhesion enough to shorten the take-off roll.
It changes magnetic heading without affecting ground forces.

questions.text: A conventional light aeroplane is hydroplaning on landing, and the wheels begin to skid under braking. What response helps restore wheel rotation while maintaining directional control?
options: Release brake pressure and use available aerodynamic controls as appropriate.
Hold the brakes locked until wheel speed becomes zero.
Increase brake pressure continuously, regardless of the skid.
Apply opposite aileron and rudder solely to use the fuselage as a brake.

questions.text: A vertical yellow sign with a black letter C is displayed at an aerodrome. Under the SERA ground-signal convention, what location does it identify?
options: The air traffic services reporting office.
The customs office.
The aircraft fuelling point.
A closed taxiway.

questions.text: A conventional TWO-BAR VASI is observed: (1) far bar red and near bar white; (2) both bars white; (3) both bars red. What are the indicated positions, respectively?
options: On the slope; above the slope; below the slope.
Below the slope; on the slope; above the slope.
On the slope; below the slope; above the slope.
Above the slope; below the slope; on the slope.

questions.text: A horizontal white landing T is displayed in the signal area. What landing direction does it indicate?
options: Parallel to the stem of the T, toward the cross-arm.
Parallel to the cross-arm, from either end.
Away from the cross-arm along the stem.
A prohibition on landing in every direction.

questions.text: A white dumb-bell in the signal area has a black bar across each circular end. Under SERA, how does this differ from an unmarked white dumb-bell?
options: Landing and take-off are confined to runways, but other manoeuvres need not be confined to runways and taxiways.
All landing, take-off and taxiing are confined to runways and taxiways.
Landing is prohibited throughout the aerodrome.
Only gliders may land while powered aircraft must remain outside.

questions.text: Under SERA, a conspicuous right-hand arrow is displayed in the aerodrome signal area. What does it instruct?
options: Make turns to the right before landing and after take-off.
Vacate the runway to the right only after landing.
Park to the right of the control tower.
Orbit continuously to the right in any part of the airspace.

questions.text: A double white cross is displayed horizontally in the aerodrome signal area. What does it indicate?
options: Sailplane flights are being performed at the aerodrome.
The runway is closed to every aircraft.
Only helicopters may use the aerodrome.
The aircraft must taxi back to its parking position.

questions.text: A horizontal red square with two yellow diagonals is displayed in the signal area. What does this signal mean?
options: Landings are prohibited.
Special caution is required but landing is permitted.
Only taxiing on hard surfaces is permitted.
A right-hand circuit is mandatory.

questions.text: A conventional tailwheel aeroplane taxis into a moderate quartering headwind from the right. Unless the AFM/POH specifies otherwise, which control positions are appropriate?
options: Right aileron up and elevator up.
Right aileron down and elevator down.
Right aileron up and elevator neutral.
Right aileron down and elevator neutral.

questions.text: A faulty magneto grounding lead is known to leave the ignition live with the switch OFF. While the aircraft awaits maintenance, which precaution addresses the immediate propeller hazard?
options: Keep people clear of the propeller and clearly warn that the ignition may remain live.
Assume the propeller is safe because the master switch is OFF.
Turn the propeller by hand to prove that the ignition is OFF.
Cover only the radio panel because the ignition needs battery power.

questions.text: The AFM pre-flight inspection specifies a quick-drain fuel strainer and sumps in each tank. Which sampling plan checks all these potential collection points?
options: Drain the strainer and every specified tank sump, checking the samples for water and contamination.
Drain only the strainer because water cannot collect in tank sumps.
Drain only one tank sump even if more are fitted.
Inspect the fuel gauge instead of obtaining samples.

questions.text: Under current aerodrome specifications, how do low-intensity obstacle lights of TypeA or TypeB indicate a fixed object?
options: By steady red lights.
By steady green lights.
By flashing blue lights.
By steady white runway-edge lights.

questions.text: A four-unit PAPI shows three white lights and one red light. Where is the aircraft relative to the indicated approach slope?
options: Slightly above the slope.
On the slope.
Slightly below the slope.
Well below the slope.

questions.text: Unless the AFM/POH specifies otherwise, how are the controls normally held when taxiing a conventional light aeroplane with a quartering tailwind from the left?
options: Left aileron down and elevator down.
Left aileron up and elevator up.
Left aileron up and elevator neutral.
Both ailerons neutral and elevator up.

questions.text: A conventional tricycle-gear aeroplane taxis into a quartering headwind from the left. Unless the AFM/POH specifies otherwise, which control positions are appropriate?
options: Left aileron up and elevator neutral.
Left aileron down and elevator down.
Left aileron down and elevator up.
Left aileron up and elevator fully up.

questions.text: At touchdown in a crosswind, what relationship helps minimise side load on the landing gear?
options: The aircraft’s longitudinal axis is aligned with its direction of travel along the runway.
The aircraft remains crabbed relative to its ground track regardless of landing-gear design.
The downwind wing is always lower regardless of drift.
The rudder is released before the wheels touch regardless of alignment.

questions.text: A light aeroplane is waiting behind a stationary jet with its engines running. Which hazard must the pilot avoid even though neither aircraft is airborne?
options: The jet-blast area behind the engines.
Only wingtip vortices produced during level flight.
Only the jet’s magnetic compass field.
Only the normal radio interference from the jet.

questions.text: A light aircraft departs from the same runway after a larger aircraft. Which plan helps avoid the larger aircraft’s wake when performance and the clearance allow it?
options: Lift off before the larger aircraft’s rotation point and stay above its departure path, turning clear when safe.
Delay lift-off until beyond the larger aircraft’s rotation point and climb below its path.
Maintain extra airspeed while flying directly through its wake.
Use an intersection behind its rotation point without considering the wake.

questions.text: When a light aircraft lands behind a larger aircraft on the same runway, which flight path and touchdown point help avoid wake turbulence?
options: Stay on or above its approach path and touch down beyond its touchdown point.
Stay below its approach path and touch down before its touchdown point.
Stay above its path but touch down before its touchdown point.
Stay below its path but touch down beyond its touchdown point.

questions.text: After a prescribed wake-separation interval has elapsed, can a pilot assume that all wake vortices have certainly disappeared?
options: No; their persistence and movement depend on wind and atmospheric conditions.
Yes; every vortex disappears exactly when the minimum interval ends.
Yes; ATC timing stops the generating aircraft from producing a wake.
Yes; vortices remain only while both aircraft are in sight.

questions.text: A paved runway portion lies before a displaced landing threshold and is marked with white arrows leading to the threshold bar. Which general use is permitted?
options: Taxiing and take-off, but not touchdown there when landing toward the displaced threshold.
Touchdown, take-off and taxiing in both directions without restriction.
Taxiing only, with no take-off use.
No aircraft movement of any kind.

questions.text: A paved blast pad or stopway beyond a runway end is marked with yellow chevrons. How should it be distinguished from the white-arrow area before a displaced threshold?
options: It is unavailable for normal taxi, take-off or landing use.
It may be used for normal take-off because it is paved.
It is the normal touchdown area for a displaced threshold.
It may always be included in the landing distance available.

questions.text: During an unavoidable off-airfield landing, how should wind direction be considered when selecting the approach?
options: Prefer a landing into wind when compatible with terrain, obstacles and a suitable landing area.
Always land exactly into wind even if that requires flying into obstacles.
Always land downwind to maximise ground speed.
Select the lowest obstacle without considering the surface or wind.

questions.text: Under Part-NCO, what condition must the first-aid kit meet in addition to being carried?
options: It must be readily accessible and kept up to date.
It may be inaccessible if its presence is listed in the aircraft log.
It need only be inspected after the aircraft changes ownership.
It must be sealed permanently, even after items are used.

questions.text: Over snow-covered ground beneath a continuous white cloud layer, diffuse light removes shadows and makes the surface merge with the sky. What is this hazard called?
options: Whiteout.
A brownout produced by dust.
A visual glide-slope indication.
The night-time autokinesis of a single light.

questions.text: After an emergency landing with a continuing fire hazard, which general evacuation direction reduces exposure to wind-carried smoke and flames?
options: Move away on the upwind side, keep clear and do not return while the area is unsafe.
Move directly downwind and stay close to the fuel tanks.
Remain beside the aircraft to recover baggage while smoke increases.
Return immediately after leaving to verify that the fire is out.

questions.text: For a Part-NCO flight near a noise-sensitive area, what is the appropriate relationship between published noise-abatement procedures and safety?
options: Take the published procedures into account, with safety having priority.
Always follow the quietest track even if it infringes obstacle clearance.
Noise abatement automatically cancels an ATC clearance.
Use an unpublished shortcut whenever it reduces flight time.

questions.text: After ditching a light aeroplane, when should occupants inflate their inflatable lifejackets?
options: Once outside the aircraft.
Before the water impact while still seated inside.
As soon as an emergency is declared inside the cabin.
Only after swimming ten metres away from the aircraft in every case.

questions.text: On a wet runway, what happens during dynamic hydroplaning at sufficiently high ground speed?
options: A water layer partly supports the tyre, reducing contact, braking and steering effectiveness.
The tyre-to-runway friction necessarily increases with speed.
The aircraft gains extra aerodynamic lift solely because the tyre is wet.
The wheel brakes become more effective as the tyre leaves the surface.

questions.text: An engine fails and a forced landing is necessary. Which task takes immediate priority over making a radio call?
options: Maintain control and establish an appropriate flight path and airspeed.
Complete the radio distress message before controlling airspeed.
Explain the entire event to the passengers before choosing a flight path.
Set every radio to 121.5 MHz before controlling the aeroplane.

questions.text: Under Part-NCO, how should the required hand extinguisher’s agent type and quantity be selected?
options: For the fire types likely in its intended compartment, while minimising toxic-gas hazard to occupants.
For the aircraft’s external paint colour only.
For every conceivable fire in any aircraft compartment without regard to occupants.
According only to whether the aeroplane has a piston or turbine engine.

questions.text: When should a pilot perform the applicable pre-flight inspection before a flight?
options: Before each flight, using the aircraft’s appropriate inspection procedure.
Only before the first flight of the day.
Only when a maintenance engineer is unavailable.
Only after the last flight of the day.

questions.text: Where the parking layout and the aircraft manual permit a choice, how is a light aeroplane generally positioned when securing it for strong forecast wind?
options: Headed into the existing or forecast wind, with appropriate tie-downs and control locks.
Tail to the wind, with tie-downs deliberately omitted.
Side-on to the wind, with every control left free.
In any direction, since parking brakes alone restrain all gust loads.

questions.text: While taxiing a high-wing tricycle-gear aeroplane in strong wind, which wind direction generally calls for particular care because it can lift the tail and the upwind wing?
options: A quartering tailwind.
A quartering headwind.
A direct headwind.
Calm air with no gusts.
